title: Data-driven architecture programme
summary: Every Cedwyn page will be generated from data: one central catalogue of the evidence feeds a small database for each area of the site, and each page is drawn from that data by one shared renderer, keeping the design visitors see today.
architecture: Central catalogue: one record per thing (evidence, artifact, place, person or public body, event, screening lead, missing record), each with a neutral description, a transcript where held, an interpretation marked as such, its source (holder, reference, date), scope tags and a public flag. Kept in the site repository as validated JSON and compiled into the site's searchable database at every build.

Area databases: each area of the site declares a selection rule; the build derives that area's own small database from the central catalogue (for example, Kissed Frogs takes every record whose scope marks it as having looked like the property but is not).

Pages from data: each page is a list of approved components bound to its area database, in the style of the open A2UI format (components as data, not code), rendered at build time by one shared renderer whose components reproduce the current design.
One switch per area: an area moves to the new path only when its pages match the old ones; switching it off restores the previous pages.
rules: A fact about the evidence is written once, in the central catalogue.
Area databases are derived, never edited by hand.
Pages hold layout only; words and records come from data.
One renderer and one set of approved components.
Only public records leave the build.
People and machine readers get the same data.
measures: Hard-coded records left on an area's pages
Pages generated from the area database
Visual match with the previous page at 390 px and desktop

flywheel: Claim one area on the task board (no two contributors on one area).
Record a baseline: screenshots at 390 px and desktop, the visible text and the records shown.
State one hypothesis: these records on this page can come from this rule and this template with no visual change.
Make the smallest change: add missing records to the catalogue, write the area rule, write the page template.
Measure: render, validate, compare with the baseline, count hard-coded records.
Keep the change only if every check passes and the numbers improve; otherwise undo it. Log the result either way.
Publish in small commits, wait for the build, check the live page at 390 px and desktop.
Record the numbers on the task board; after three failed attempts on one area, log the blocker and move on.
audit: 44 source themes in 36 visitor areas: 12 are snapshots of separate apps, 15 are hand-written pages, 14 mix a data file with pre-made pages, 2 are built by their own tools and 1 is generated from data. Three partial databases exist today; none is yet the single source the pages read.
sources: A2UI open project and specification v0.9.1 (a2ui.org; a2ui-project on GitHub)
